stories.title: CDA directs removal of 'unauthorised' construction, guard post at JUI-F chief's residence in Islamabad
summary: The notice affixed outside the residence of the JUI-F chief — addressed to the legal owner of the property and dated Oct 30 (Friday) — highlighted three violations under the Islamabad Capital Territory Building Control Regulations 2020 (amended 2023).
It pointed out illegal and unauthorised construction in building setbacks (open spaces), a guard post built on CDA land, and a generator on CDA land.
Meanwhile, after the notice was issued, Maulana Asjad Mahmood, the son of the JUI-F chief, claimed it was retaliation for pointing out alleged encroachments by a senior military official.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

stories.title: Ogra notifies 15.3pc increase in RLNG price for October
summary: According to the notification, RLNG’s sale price for SNGPL at the transmission stage increased by 13.9pc to $15.94 per mmBtu for October compared to $13.99 per mmBtu in September.
Meanwhile, RLNG sale price for SSGCL has been increased at the transmission stage by 15.25pc to $14.53 per mmBtu for October, against $12.611 per mmBtu in September.
The sale price at the distribution stage for the company thus also increased by 15.27pc to $16.396 per mmBtu for October compared to $14.22 in September.

stories.title: Pakistani three-wheelers go international as automotive manufacturer opens plant in Philippines
summary: In a post on the social media platform X, the Pakistan embassy in the Southeast Asian country said: “Pakistan-made three-wheelers have entered the Philippine market!” It said that Philippine President Ferdinand R.
Marcos Jr inaugurated the assembly plant of Pakistan’s Sazgar Engineering Works Limited.

He said that the plant was designed to assemble approximately 12,000 three-wheeled vehicles annually, covering both electric and internal combustion engines. “Sazgar has been building vehicles in Pakistan for over three decades.

stories.title: Over 30 shops gutted as fire rips through furniture market in Karachi's Gulistan-i-Johar
summary: KARACHI: Over 30 shops were destroyed when a blaze erupted at a furniture market in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar in the early hours of Friday.
Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan said the fire erupted in a furniture market near Kamran Chowrangi.
In September, at least three people suffered minor injuries from smoke inhalation after a huge fire erupted in a factory at the Karachi EPZ, near Landhi Industrial Area.

stories.title: PPP delegation calls on Senate opposition leader, urges participation in proposed committee on electoral reforms
summary: On Friday, another PPP delegation, comprising the party’s secretary general Nayyar Bokhari, Senator Waqar Mehdi, Nadeem Afzal Chan and Rehman, visited Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas with yet another invitation to join the proposed body.

A day earlier, another PPP delegation invited Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms.
The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”.

stories.title: NA adopts resolution stating workplace harassment not only sexual in nature, may manifest in gender discrimination
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Assembly on Friday approved a resolution reaffirming that workplace harassment was not limited to conduct of a sexual nature but may also include intimidation, humiliation and gender-based discrimination.

It underscored that workplace harassment was not limited to conduct of a sexual nature, but “may also manifest through gender-based discrimination, intimidation, humiliation, degrading treatment, hostile behaviour and misuse of authority, whether sexual or non-sexual in nature”.

The resolution concluded by reaffirming that a workplace free from harassment, humiliation and gender-based discrimination was “not a privilege, but a fundamental requirement of human dignity, equality and justice”.

stories.title: Salman Ali Agha hopes Pakistan top-order turns up in tri-series final, seeks ‘perfect game’
summary: Pakistan batter Salman Ali Agha believes the the side have not yet displayed a complete team performance in the ongoing One-day International tri-nation series, and hopes the final against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday is where it falls into place.
The hosts’ top-order has been notably starved of runs for the series, underscoring Pakistan’s underwhelming campaign with the bat. “Sometimes all of your players don’t score runs.
The fragility of Pakistan’s top order is just one of the factors that have gone into the slightly unconvincing cricket the side has played in this series, even in the matches they have won.

stories.title: CDF Munir, Singapore's FM discuss regional security and bilateral cooperation
summary: During the meeting, CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening bilateral relations with Singapore, including enhancing “institutional linkages and constructive engagement for promoting regional peace, stability and security”.

Dar and Balakrishnan also discussed cooperation at multilateral fora and Pakistan’s enhanced engagement with Asean, particularly in the context of Singapore’s forthcoming chairmanship of the body in 2027.

Delegation-level talks Later, their opening remarks from delegation-level talks between the two sides were televised, with Dar saying that the depth of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and Singapore was not reflected in economic ties.

stories.title: Govt increases diesel price by Rs2.29, petrol remains unchanged until Nov 2
summary: According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol will continue to be sold at Rs377.91 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs402.96 per litre from Oct 31 to Nov 2.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs.

stories.title: Bill proposing quarterly gas pricing lands in Senate
summary: ISLAMABAD: In what is set to stir a new controversy, a bill proposing quarterly determination of natural gas prices landed in the upper House of Parliament on Friday.

The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced in the House by Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry at a time when the daily fuel pricing mechanism has drawn widespread criticism.
The bill also empowers the federal government to advise Ogra to carry forward the entire or part of a quarterly adjustment to its forthcoming half-yearly determination under Section 8.

stories.title: 'I will never go back to sea': 11 fishermen released from Indian captivity reunite with families in Karachi
summary: KARACHI: 11 Pakistani fishermen, after spending several years in Indian jails for unknowingly crossing over to Indian waters while fishing, were reunited with their families in Karachi on Friday morning.

Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi Asked how his boat crossed over to the other side, he said that they experienced an engine failure, following which the boat drifted towards Indian waters.
Pakistani fishermen reunite with families at Edhi Centre on October 30. — White Star/ Fahim Siddiqi “He served his sentence two years ago, but still he has not returned home.

stories.title: ISPR spokesperson says Pakistan ‘cautiously optimistic’ on Iran-US mediation, warns against spoilers
summary: Also Read: CDF Munir meets senior Iranian officials as Pakistan continues diplomatic push to end conflict Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief ​Ibrahim Kalin joined CDF Munir in Tehran on Monday.
The wording of the pact does not bar new members, Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join. “Anyone who has a shared vision of collective ‌deterrence and ⁠regional peace, why not?
Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership.

stories.title: Spanish transport minister refuses to resign over second major train crash on his watch
summary: Spain’s transport minister on Friday rejected calls for his resignation over the second train accident on his watch to cause mass casualties this year, as authorities worked to identify the victims from a crash that left at least 69 dead.

Authorities can’t rule out more fatalities No additional bodies were found when rescue teams overturned a train carriage on Thursday, Castilla-La Mancha regional leader Emiliano Garcia-Page said on TVE.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Friday vowed to find out what caused the accident. “It is unacceptable for a country like Spain, with such a strong high-speed rail system, to suffer two accidents of this nature and magnitude in a single year,” he said.

stories.title: Pakistan Army destroys Afghan Taliban posts in response to firing at Angoor Adda: state media
summary: It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.
Around mid-October, the state media reported that security forces had again responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in KP’s Upper Kurram.
It quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”.

stories.title: PSL franchises allowed seven retentions, must release top-tier player if maximum limit exercised
summary: The provision, unanimously approved by all eight franchises at a tournament operations workshop at Gaddafi Stadium on Thursday, is among the key regulations finalised ahead of the PSL 12 player auction scheduled for January 23.
The auction, which will be only the second in PSL history, will operate under a salary cap of Rs45 crore for each franchise.

The regulations were finalised during a workshop chaired by PSL chief executive Salman Naseer, with all eight franchises reaching unanimous agreement after reviewing the auction rules clause by clause.

stories.title: FCC says not implementing SC's verdicts amounts to 'challenging the very framework of the legal system'
summary: On Friday, FCC judge, Justice Ali Baqar Najafi, emphasised that the orders of the SC, as the then-apex court before the 27th Constitutional Amendment, were “not merely recommendations or advisories but they are legal mandate that must be followed”.

Justice Najafi was a member of a three-judge bench, which was headed by FCC Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan, that had taken up a set of contempt of court petitions on the non-implementation of the SC judgement.

Reverting to the case, the FCC noted that the SC judgement required that the beneficiary employees would have to undergo relevant tests applicable to their post to be conducted by the Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC) within three months.

stories.title: K-P govt says evidence being gathered against Sohail Afridi over alleged corruption
summary: Speaking at a press conference at the Information Cell in the Civil Secretariat on Friday, she said the government was pursuing institutional reforms, transparency and improved public service delivery.
Inspections of government and private schools and seminaries across the province had identified 4,049 educational institutions requiring repairs and rehabilitation.
Concluding, Bilour said the government’s vision was not merely a slogan but a commitment to good governance, institutional reforms, accountability, transparency and public service.

stories.title: Asia chip firms see strong AI demand; market jitters continue
summary: Asian chip supply chain companies said on Friday ‌that AI-related demand remained strong, while investor concerns persisted over whether the massive investments in AI infrastructure would generate adequate returns.
The company, on Friday, forecast a stronger-than-expected 87% jump in operating profit to 1.17 trillion yen ($7.41 billion), underscoring robust demand for chipmaking equipment.

"It will take time to fix this week's selloff." Tokyo Electron, a major ​supplier of equipment ⁠for processes such as deposition and etching to chipmakers, said it would spend up to 150 billion yen to buy back some 25 million shares.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to boost cooperation in oil, refineries and minerals
summary: Both sides underscored that the strong defence and strategic partnership between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia provides a foundation for broader regional peace, stability and economic cooperation.

Malik invited Saudi Arabia’s Vice Minister of Mining, Khalid al-Mudafier, to attend the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum, scheduled to be held in Islamabad on November 12 and 13, highlighting further opportunities for cooperation and investment in Pakistan’s minerals sector.
The minister assured the ambassador that Pakistan deeply valued its historic relationship with Saudi Arabia and remained committed to expanding cooperation across strategic sectors.

stories.title: Meta, TikTok, X lose legal challenge against UK watchdog over online safety data demands
summary: TikTok and X lost a legal challenge against British regulator Ofcom on ‌Friday over information requests made under the Online Safety Act, in one of the first tests of Britain's nascent online safety regime.
Friday's ⁠decision by London's High Court is a boost for Ofcom, though a potentially more significant ​ruling on Meta's separate case about how Ofcom calculates fees and potential fines is awaited.

Meta, which is ​also challenging Ofcom over the categorisation of WhatsApp in the new regime, was made the subject of Ofcom's first formal investigation under the Online Safety Act earlier this month.

stories.title: CDA gives Fazlur Rehman's residence 15 days to remove alleged encroachments
summary: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday issued an encroachment notice at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, identifying illegal constructions and encroachments on its land and directing their removal within 15 days.
Meanwhile, Fazl's son and JUI-F leader Maulana Asjad Mahmood described the action as retaliatory, linking it to his father's political differences with the government.

He regretted that the matter was being used to secure political gains, saying the CDA had been taking action against encroachments and illegal constructions in Islamabad for over a year, beginning with the city's posh sectors.

stories.title: Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3bn 'complex' security breach
summary: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Friday it was working to resolve a “complex attack” that hit around $6.3 billion in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft.

Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said Thursday it had “high confidence” that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing “robust on and off-chain intelligence.” “Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists,” TRM said.
Crypto prices tumble For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.

stories.title: Netanyahu's bloc finishes ahead in Israel election, but well short of majority
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from general election showed on Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote.

The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar.
Netanyahu had tried during the voting to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash, and Likud peddled the accusations throughout Thursday.

stories.title: FBI and US Secret Service working with Binance after $6.3 billion hack, source says
summary: Binance is ‌working with law enforcement around the world, including the Federal ​Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and ​the United States Secret Service (USSS), ⁠after hackers stole a ​record $6.3 billion from the platform, ​a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.
TRM added 8 listed crypto addresses under sanctions.
The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most ‌of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.

stories.title: Short-term inflation rises to 11.32pc in last week of October, driven by perishable food prices
summary: Short-term inflation has remained in double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum and diesel prices.
The data showed that of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, the prices of 15 commodities increased, while those of 12 items declined.
Last week, short-term inflation rose to 11.85pc year-on-year, driven largely by higher wheat flour prices, according to data released by the PBS.

stories.title: PTI K-P division dispels impression of internal discord
summary: In a statement issued after the meeting, the parliamentary party said, “The parliamentary party expressed complete confidence in the leadership of Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and clarified that there is no grouping of any kind in Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf.

According to the statement issued by PTI K-P on X, the meeting also decided that the provincial parliamentary party would be given effective representation in any future protest movement, negotiations or political strategy.

The federal government imposed emergency and governor's rule in K-P under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.

stories.title: Experts urge govts to treat manosphere and misogyny as public health issues: report
summary: Online misogyny and the growing influence of the so-called manosphere should be addressed as a public health issue rather than treated solely as a problem of social media regulation, according to a new viewpoint published in The Lancet.

The authors argue that the online ecosystem, which includes communities promoting anti-feminist beliefs, male victimhood and hostile attitudes towards women, is contributing to a range of social and health-related harms.

Their recommendations include improving access to mental health services for boys and young men, strengthening school-based education, promoting healthier representations of masculinity and making social media platforms more accountable for the content their algorithms amplify.

stories.title: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses
summary: Multiple drone strikes have hit northern regions of Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians, including children, witnesses and a medical source told AFP on Friday.
In Amhara, a witness said four drone strikes "were carried out one after another" on Thursday on a camp for displaced people.

The ACLED conflict monitor said the drone strike was "believed to have been carried out by the ENDF (Ethiopian National Defence Force)... killing 12 civilians and injuring an unspecified number of people".

stories.title: New York state police to investigate sexual assault complaints at Cornell University
summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has announced an agreement allowing state police to investigate sexual assault complaints at Cornell University, following criticism of the institution’s handling of a former student’s allegation that she was gang-raped at a fraternity house.

Under the agreement signed by Cornell University and New York State Police on Thursday, survivors who decide to pursue criminal charges can choose whether state police or Cornell University Police will lead their investigations.
Separately, former US Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates was appointed to lead an independent review of Cornell’s handling of sexual misconduct complaints.

stories.title: Erling Haaland, Little Simz among winners of Instagram Rings Awards 2026
summary: Football superstar Erling Haaland, British rapper Little Simz, American footwear designer Salehe Bembury and comedian Jordan Firstman are among the international personalities recognised at Instagram's Rings Awards 2026.

Announced on Thursday, the awards celebrate 25 creators from around the world whose work demonstrates originality, creative risk-taking and cultural influence across fashion, sport, music, comedy, design and entertainment.

With personalities from football, music, fashion, comedy and visual arts sharing the honours, the 2026 Instagram Rings Awards underline how creativity and cultural influence can take many different forms.

stories.title: Court grants NCCIA four-day physical remand of suspect in counterfeit US postage stamp scam
summary: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Friday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) a further four-day physical remand of the prime suspect in a Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps.
The NCCIA produced suspect Faheem Akram and his co-suspect, Naeem, before the court after their previous four-day remand expired.
The initial investigation revealed that the suspect had allegedly been operating a website since August 2023 through which he sold more than five million counterfeit US postage labels online.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia agree to deepen cooperation in oil and energy sector
summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on Friday agreed to further strengthen cooperation in oil storage, refinery upgradation, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) supplies and minerals.
The understanding was reached during a meeting between Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Saudi Ambassador to Pakistan Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy in Islamabad.
The prime minister said, “Pakistan stands shoulder-to-shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity.”

stories.title: LHC directs Noreen Niazi’s counsel to file separate plea for medical treatment, family meetings
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court on Friday directed the counsel for Noreen Niazi, sister of former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan, to file a separate miscellaneous application seeking medical treatment and family meetings.

Justice Abher Gul Khan issued the direction while hearing a petition filed by Sakeena Niazi challenging the extension of the preventive detention of PTI founder Imran Khan’s two sisters, Noreen and Dr Uzma Khan.

The detention had come amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party had called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.

stories.title: Six killed in helicopter crash in Indian Himalayan state, ANI says
summary: Six people were killed in a helicopter crash in the Indian Himalayan state of Uttarakhand on Friday, news agency ANI reported, citing an official from the state's civil aviation authority.

The helicopter was flying from Badrinath, a prominent pilgrimage destination for Hindus located in the mountains, to Dehradun city, the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) said in a statement.
Earlier, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said his ‌office ⁠had received information about a helicopter crashing near a village in the Joshimath area.

stories.title: Pakistan seek perfect finish to tri-series
summary: A gruelling battle is expected as Pakistan take on Sri Lanka in the ODI tri-series final at the Gaddafi Stadium Lahore on Saturday.

Pakistan, who suffered an eight-wicket defeat against Sri Lanka in their last league match, have had two successive days of training and are expected to have worked hard on addressing their weaknesses.
Pakistan's senior batsman Salman Ali Agha said the team could win the final if they played to their full potential.

stories.title: Politics casts shadow over Olympic sport
summary: IOC president Kirsty Coventry's desire is that "politics does not take over on the field of play", but Ukraine and former executives from her organisation have told AFP that politics and sport remain inseparable.

"Until that moment, isolation is not political -- it is a matter of basic human decency." Former International Olympic Committee marketing executive Terrence Burns told AFP that globally speaking, "sport has never been separate from politics".
"The boycott agenda of the eighties very nearly destroyed the Olympic movement," Michael Payne, a former IOC marketing chief, told AFP.

stories.title: Cop martyred in KP's Bajaur as terrorists attack police post: official
summary: BAJAUR: A police officer was martyred after terrorists attacked a police post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur district, officials said on Friday.
The attack on the police post in Silai Pati area in the remote Barang tehsil, bordering Malakand district, occurred late on Thursday night.

Mansoor Khan, a spokesperson for the district police, while confirming the attack, told Dawn that a group of Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists targeted the Silai Pati police post, prompting the personnel to retaliate bravely and courageously.

stories.title: Rubio hosts G20 ministers as Iran, Ukraine wars divide members
summary: Few breakthroughs are expected this week from the Group of 20 economies -- which include China, India, Russia, Japan, Germany and France -- as officials face divisions over Moscow's war on Ukraine and fallout from conflict with Iran.

Rubio's encounter with Lavrov -- whose presence adds an additional layer of tension -- will be closely watched as Washington pursues diplomacy on Ukraine while seeking Moscow's cooperation on reining in fuel prices, a key campaign issue in the midterms.

Also read: US irks G20 ministers by bringing back Russia, barring journalists Trump has eased some sanctions on Moscow recently while touting a deal for Russia to sell diesel as prices soared, squeezing Americans.

stories.title: Aima Baig revisits ‘Sajna Door’ in heartfelt tribute to fans
summary: Singer Aima Baig has revisited her much-loved song Sajna Door, sharing a spontaneous rendition on Instagram to thank fans for keeping the track popular years after its release.
View this post on Instagram Baig also hinted at a possible live session, promising to go live soon so she and her fans could sing the song together.
Originally released as part of the soundtrack for the 2018 Pakistani romantic action-comedy Teefa in Trouble, Sajna Door features vocals by Baig and singer-songwriter Ali Zafar.
